dishes.name: Ankara tava
dishes.desc: Lamb and rice baked slowly in a shallow dish until the top crisps. The city's own celebration dish, found in old lokantas around Ulus.

dishes.name: Beypazarı kurusu
dishes.desc: Thin, hard twice-baked biscuits from the town of Beypazarı, eaten with tea or crumbled into soup. The best-known local product of the area.

dishes.name: Ankara simit
dishes.desc: Sesame-crusted bread ring sold from carts and bakeries across the city. The Ankara version is thinner and crunchier than the Istanbul one.

dishes.name: Beypazarı güveç
dishes.desc: Meat and vegetables stewed for hours in a sealed clay pot in a wood oven. Beypazarı's old bakeries still cook it the slow way.

dishes.name: Keskin tava
dishes.desc: Lamb slow-roasted on a tray until it falls apart, from the town of Keskin near Kırıkkale, served with bread to mop up the juices.
